for a multiserver loss model, the indirect estimator based on the mean occupancy is much more efficient than the direct estimator based on the number of customers in the system when the system loading is high, and the computational effort required to obtain a given statistical precision is independent of the system size.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
for a given system size, a good choice of the blocking probability to estimate is a relatively large one, and a good estimator is one based on the indirect approach.

the asymptotic variance formulas are very accurate, that the computational effort is inversely proportional to system size, and that the time to approach the steady state is negligible for small to moderately sized systems.
for a fixed blocking probability, the computational effort to obtain good statistical estimates of the blocking probability decreases as the system size grows.
The main takeaway from our work is that
simulation experiments to estimate steady-state blocking probabilities can be designed to be much more efficient than is commonly believed, even for large systems.
simulation run lengths can be determined before the simulation has even been run, and the computational effort can be reduced by using the appropriate estimator, depending on the load.
simulation experiments can be designed more efficiently, and can provide more reliable results, when the asymptotic variance formula is used to determine the required run length.
